name: Unicode
summary: A character-encoding standard that assigns code points to characters and symbols.
description: Unicode provides a common coded character set. Encodings such as UTF-8 define how Unicode code points are represented as bytes.
facts: A Unicode code point is written using the U+ notation.
A code point is an abstract number and is not itself a byte sequence.

name: UTF-8
summary: A variable-width encoding for Unicode code points.
description: UTF-8 represents Unicode code points using sequences of one to four bytes and preserves ASCII byte values for the ASCII range.
facts: ASCII characters use one byte in UTF-8.

name: Byte Sequence
summary: An ordered series of eight-bit values used to represent or transmit data.
description: A byte sequence gives software a concrete representation for text, numbers, files and network messages. Its interpretation depends on an agreed format or protocol.
facts: The same bytes can have different meanings under different formats.
Serialization turns structured values into a byte sequence.

name: Serialization
summary: The process of converting structured data into a representation suitable for storage or transmission.
description: Serialization defines how values and structure become bytes or text. Deserialization reconstructs values according to the same format.
facts: A serializer and deserializer must agree on a format.
JSON is one possible serialization format.

name: JSON
summary: A text format for serializing structured values.
description: JSON represents objects, arrays, strings, numbers, booleans and null. Its interoperable grammar is defined by RFC 8259.
facts: A JSON object contains name-value pairs.
A JSON array is an ordered sequence of values.

name: Structured Data
summary: Data organized according to an explicit model of fields, values or relationships.
description: Structured data can be validated, queried and serialized because its organization is known to producers and consumers.
facts: A schema can constrain the allowed structure.
Relationships can connect records into a graph.

name: File
summary: A named sequence of bytes managed by a file system.
description: Applications interpret file bytes according to a format. A database file can contain pages, records, indexes and metadata.
facts: A filename does not by itself determine the content format.
File formats define how bytes are interpreted.

name: Database
summary: An organized collection of data managed for durable access and queries.
description: A database system coordinates data representation, retrieval and updates. Some systems use tree indexes to locate records efficiently.
facts: A database may persist data in one or more files.
Indexes trade additional storage and update work for faster lookup.

name: B-tree
summary: A balanced search-tree family designed to keep ordered keys in blocks.
description: B-trees reduce storage accesses by keeping many keys and child references in each node. Database systems commonly use related structures for indexes.
facts: All leaves remain at the same depth in a balanced B-tree.
